steps.text: Make sauerkraut filling: Melt butter in a skillet over medium heat. Cook and stir onion in hot butter until translucent, about 5 minutes. Add sauerkraut and cook, stirring occasionally, for 5 more minutes. Season with salt and pepper, then remove to a plate to cool.

Make potato filling: Melt butter in the same skillet over medium heat. Cook and stir onion in hot butter until translucent, about 5 minutes. Stir in mashed potatoes, salt, and white pepper. Remove from heat.
Make dough: Beat together sour cream and eggs in a large bowl until smooth. Sift flour, baking powder, and salt into a separate bowl; stir into sour cream mixture until dough comes together.
Knead dough on a lightly floured surface until firm and smooth.
Divide dough in half, then roll out one half to 1/8-inch thickness. Cut into 3-inch rounds using a biscuit cutter. Place a small spoonful of potato filling into the center of each round.
Moisten edges with water, fold over, and press with a fork to seal. Roll and fill remaining dough half with sauerkraut filling.
Bring a large pot of lightly salted water to a boil. Add pierogies in batches to boiling water and cook until they float to the top, 3 to 5 minutes. Remove with a slotted spoon.

raw_recipe.headline: Pierogi (Polish Dumplings)
raw_recipe.description: These pierogies, made with tender sour cream and egg dough, are stuffed with buttery mashed potato, onion, and sauerkraut to make Polish dumplings.

review.reviewBody: Being Polish, and born in Poland, I have had many pierogi's in my day. After many disappointing pierogi meals, I came across this recipe...and all I can say is YUM! My kids (who do not care for dad's food preferences) inhaled these and asked for more. Great recipe -Dziekujemy! All this talk about Pierogi's is making me hungry.

I have only ever had the frozen kind in the grocery stores. THIS WAS SOO MUCH BETTER!! The only thing I did was use 1/2 Tbs of Baking Powder per recommendations. 
I used my kitchen aid to mix and knead the dough. 

I worked in small batches and did not find it as hard to work when rolling out. meaning, instead of trying to roll "half" the dough at one time, I floured my working surface, only grabbed a handful of dough, sprinkled flour on top, flattened with my hand, sometimes I had to sprinkle a bit more flour, then rolled out & cut. When dealing with "sticky" dough, it is better to work in small batches. 
Before sealing, I wet the edges (like I do for pie crusts) and pressed them together. Sprinkled flour on a plate as I stacked them to prevent them from sticking to each other. 

I have also put them on wax paper in the freezer while I am making them. 
I've never had an issue with the dough, being too sticky or anything, and I have never had them open up while boiling. 

We stuff ours with homemade mashed potatoes, onions and rinsed & drained small curd cottage cheese. 

Boil till they reach the top, the fry in butter. 
Eat as is or top them with Sour Cream and Bacon. Sometimes diced Jalepenos. 

My family of 8 loves these.

I have made this lots of times I use 1/4 cup melt butter, 1/2 cup sour cream, 1/4 cup warm milk all the rest I make 5-6 batches of dough I make boil and freeze, I also freeze any unused dough you candy bring out after a year and allow it to defrost it will be as soft as the first day you made, I make all of these all m By my self I'm 75 years old Mickey D

The dough recipe is excellent!! For best results knead the dough with a dough hook for 5 minutes.
 If you like cheese in with the potato filling use Cooper Sharp. I buy a chunk and grate it with a box grater. The Cooper Sharp really makes them outstanding
There’s no reason to dirty a bowl just to sift the dry ingredients into. Sift them directly into the egg/sour cream mixture

This review is just for the dough for the perogies. This was my first time making perogies, and the dough turned out great. I had to add a bit more flour, but other than that I didn't change a thing. I found when rolling out the dough, you should roll it a bit thinner, it's springy. I let the dough rest while I made the potato filling. When filling the rounds, I first wet the edges, then stretched it a bit as I folded it over. Make sure no filling is between the edges when you seal them. I found adding a bit of flour as I sealed them worked well. I placed the finished perogies on a floured silicone mat and let them set before cooking them. They had a great texture. I will definitely be making these again.

I'm Polish and we adapted our dough recipe using this recipe by adding sour cream to our dough. It makes it more pliable. 
For the sauerkraut filling, we always rinse our sauerkraut, otherwise it's way too sour. We chop the sauerkraut but you could also put it in a food processor to get rid of the long strings of cabbage. We sauté chopped onions in butter then add the sauerkraut, salt and pepper. It really only needs to be warmed. 
Once the pierogi are boiled in water, we drain them and add them to a pan with browned saltine cracker crumbs in butter. That's how our family makes them. We've never made them using any other filling. We freeze them to heat up throughout the year. My mom and I make these together once a year and share with family during the holidays.

I love pierogies! A Polish neighbor showed me how to make these and although takes time, worth it. We made ours with mashed potatoes, small diced onions and cheese as a filling. Plus caramelized onions and sour cream for the topping. She also browned the pierogies after boiling-in butter of course!

Unlike many other reviewers, my grandmother's pierogies came from the freezer section at the grocery store, so I don't have anything to compare this to. We really enjoyed these, although they are a lot of work. I needed a nap after making them. I fried them with bacon and onions after boiling them. The person who suggested freezing them first to prevent them from splitting open was 100% right! None of mine opened. Boil them 6-10 min if you are freezing them first. I agree with others that 1/4 tsp salt for the dough isn't enough. I don't like salty food, but this was way too bland. I would use 1/2 tsp next time.

I made this recipe for a Superbowl party. Being the only Steelers fan I felt the need to bring something Pittsburgh-style. I made them ahead of time, sauteed in butter/onions, and poured it all into a crock pot with a little extra butter. The were pretty much gone by the end of the first quarter. Nothing but compliments!

I just added another notch to my culinary belt with this one! My husband said they were the best pierogi he has ever had. Now for the details: I used this recipe for the dough only, making my own fillings of mashed potato and Monterey Jack, and another of mashed sweet potato. I followed the dough recipe as described, but found it VERY sticky. Make sure you have at least a cup or 2 extra of flour to add and keep the surface covered. I rolled out portions of dough and cut with a ravioli cutter, laying on a cookie sheet coated with flour (lots of flour to keep from sticking). I put my potato mix in ziplock bags and cut the corner, piping a small blob on each dough circle, brushed the edges with water and sealed with a fork. I transferred to another sheet with flour, finishing all. Made about 2 dozen with a 3" cutter. I put the pan of pierogi into the freezer for a few hours. To serve, Boiled for a 5 minutes or so in a large pan of water then plopped into a pan of sautéed onions and butter to fry up a bit. I served with a big scoop of butter and onion and a dollop of sour cream. Perfection!
By the way, "pierogi" is already plural. "Pierogies" is laughable. One is a pieróg. One pieróg and several pierogi.
Yum
I will definitely try your recipe but I would love to see you prep in only 25 minutes!!!
I grew up with this dish and still make them often.

Followed this recipe and it was easy and fantastic! Didn’t change anything and followed the recipe exactly. The cool thing is this recipe is a fantastic base recipe and if you want to add cheese, bacon, etc. the sky’s the limit :)

The heck with frying, boiling pierogis. I brought the oven to 425 degrees, brushed them with olive oil, and baked for 20 minutes. And, they store well when wrapped in good old wax paper and scotch tape the tip of the paper.
The dough was a gooey mess. I followed the instructions, but it was not good at all. The dough was was weak and difficult to work with.
